newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium spread narrows on LME, July tightens.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium spread narrows on LME, July tightens.

text.p: Tightness in London Metal Exchange (LME) July aluminium dates is exerting pressure on the overall cash/threes contango, which by Monday was significantly below financing levels.
Traders said the developing tightness, which is still some way off, is largely due to technical factors, following an early-April sell-off.
"This looks to me to be technical more than anything else...I'm not sure if there is anybody behind it," one trader said.
Cash/threes traded at a $24 contango, against levels above $30 last last week, with the crunch period seen from the start of July. June/July was showing a minimal $2 contango.
Traders said the tight dates on the LME range from the start of July to July 11, and probably reflect short positions put on in early April.
During the period April 3 to April 14, three months aluminium prices fell sharply under investment selling, dropping by $100 from levels in the mid-$1,640s.
Since then the market has recovered strongly, and at one stage on Monday was up around $1,640, while some of the shorts have covered.
"I assume those people have been covering, and it is a bit of a double hit -- the market is up and the spread has come in," another trader said.
The price rise is taking place against consistent declines in LME warehouse stocks.
Last week the overall drawdown was 18,750 tonnes, while total stocks stand at 807,225 tonnes, down 125,300 so far this year.
Although the contango has whipped in over the past few days, aluminium has largely been financeable this year, with cash/threes mostly around $31/32.
There has been some talk recently of financing deals, with metal moving off-warrant, while long-term financing would imply that significant tonnages are not readily available.
If there is further covering to be done, spreads may well tighten further nearer July, they said.
